title: Transient Caution During a Flight Phase Transition — Fault Symptom
abstract: Fault symptom procedure for a transient caution seen by the crew during a take-off, approach or landing phase transition, and the checks that establish whether the inhibit standard explains it.

sections.purpose: Fault symptom procedure for a crew report of a caution that appears briefly during a flight phase transition and clears without action, with no associated system fault recorded.
sections.fault_description: The crew report a caution during the take-off acceleration segment, or during a configuration change on approach, that clears within a few seconds and leaves no maintenance message describing a system fault. The parameters involved are legitimately transient at those points in the flight. This is a documentation and configuration question rather than a system fault, and the first task is to establish which inhibit standard the aircraft carries, because three standards are in service and each inhibits a different set.
sections.isolation_procedure: 1. Obtain the crew report and establish the flight phase and the caution text as reported. 2. Read the flight warning computer software and configuration part numbers from the maintenance terminal. 3. Establish which inhibit standard those part numbers correspond to. 4. Where the caution is in the inhibited set for a later standard than the one fitted, the report is explained by configuration and the applicable bulletin should be scheduled. No component action is required. 5. Where the aircraft carries the latest standard and the caution is still reported, check that both computers carry the same part numbers; a mismatched pair inhibits according to the lower standard. 6. Where the pair matches, read the parameter recording for the reported transition and confirm whether the parameter genuinely exceeded its threshold. 7. Where it did, the report is a real system transient and the isolation continues in the chapter of the system concerned, not here. 8. Where it did not, report the case with the recording attached; a caution with no parameter excursion indicates an inhibit table defect and is handled as a service query.
sections.dispatch_note: No dispatch consequence. A transient caution that has been explained by the inhibit standard is not a defect and does not require deferral. Where both computers carry mismatched software the aircraft is dispatchable, but the mismatch must be corrected at the next opportunity because the inhibit behaviour is then not the one described to the crew.

type_data.fault_symptom: Transient caution reported during take-off, approach or landing phase transition

possible_causes.cause: Aircraft at an earlier inhibit standard than the reported caution requires
Mismatched software part numbers between the two computers
Genuine parameter excursion in the system concerned

dispatch.dispatch_condition: No dispatch restriction; software mismatch to be corrected at the next opportunity
